topic.source_contract: Planning noise, acoustic design, agent-of-change and permit-noise evidence

facts.guard: numerical criteria are not rigid universal thresholds

facts.agent_of_change: new sensitive development may need suitable mitigation near established uses
facts.guard: planning and pollution-control regimes have separate roles
one regime's record is not substituted for another decision
permit evidence is not automatically a planning acoustic assessment

facts.use: screen whether permit application needs impact assessment and management plan
facts.guard: tool output does not grant a permit or planning permission

scope_guards: Noise-generating development and noise-sensitive development are assessed from different directions.
Current and permitted-but-not-yet-occurring activities must be considered where relevant.
SOAEL, LOAEL and amenity concepts require context and are not universal parcel scores.
Good acoustic design should be considered early; insulation alone is not assumed sufficient.
The agent of change must identify existing impacts and suitable mitigation but this does not guarantee no complaints.
Planning, environmental permitting, strategic noise mapping and statutory nuisance are separate regimes.
Numerical criteria are not applied as rigid thresholds in every circumstance.
No score or promotion is written without exact receptors, source operations, baseline survey, acoustic model, mitigation and planning evidence.
